The role:
Join us as a Product Engineer to build a new product within Brevo called Brevo OS.

Brevo OS is a startup inside Brevo: a team of six, a product we started from an empty repository earlier this year, and the feel of a small company within the big one. The product works, the first customer deployments are beginning, and a great deal is still undecided — so the people who join us now will shape what it becomes.

It's an AI-native operating system for small businesses: a system of agents that helps a solopreneur, a hair salon or a building contractor run their whole business — clients, contracts and signature, invoicing, their website, their inbox. Modules get added the way an ERP grows, except the whole thing is built around agents from the ground up.

Your Impact at Brevo:

  • Turn a very high level business need into something real : understand the function, define the users, the smallest useful version, the entities and their lifecycles, the permissions and constraints that matter, and what to build versus integrate
  • Decide which of our platform primitives to extend rather than reinvent, then build it, ship it, watch it in production, and improve it
  • Work across product management, frontend, backend, data modelling, infrastructure, and AI. Everyone arrived with a specialism and nobody is confined to theirs; product thinking and business analysis is part of everyone’s job
  • Build almost entirely through coding agents: Claude Code is the workflow, not a pilot running alongside it, for implementation, codebase exploration, documentation, debugging, and operations
  • Decompose problems into work an agent can actually execute, give it context without over-constraining it, and tell the difference between correct and merely plausible
  • Verify with tests and instrumentation, not vibes, and keep a large generated codebase coherent
  • Work day to day in TypeScript, Kubernetes, and agentic frameworks



Who you are:

  • Around 2-5 years of professional engineering experience. We care more about your slope than your years
  • Real depth in something, and no attachment to staying there. Bring what you're genuinely strong at — the team compounds those — and expect to spend a good part of your time well outside it
  • Coding agents already central to how you work. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, something equivalent. Not "I've generated the Unit Tests" — real delegation of substantial work, and real review of what comes back. Scepticism about generated output is a feature of this job, not a problem
  • Evidence you've owned a problem, not just implemented a ticket — something you helped define, drove, shipped and then lived with in production. Product questions are your questions too
  • At your best when the brief is one sentence and the plan is still moving. We're learning what this product is, so priorities change often. The mission doesn't
  • English. We're an international team working across France and India, and English is our working language. French is not required



If you don't meet all the requirements above but believe this opportunity matches your expectations and experience, we still encourage you to apply!

Why people love working at Brevo:

  • A place to grow, together: Join an international team in a bright, collaborative office located in a vibrant neighbourhood
  • Practical perks for everyday balance: RTT days off, 50% public transport reimbursement, Sustainable Mobility Package (whether you ride a classic bike or go electric, we support your choice to commute greener) and daily Swile meal vouchers (€12.50/day)
  • Learning, every step of the way: Access to English classes and 155,000+ courses on Udemy, plus a strong internal culture of knowledge-sharing and support
  • Flexible for life: A remote-friendly setup, budget to support your home workspace, and relocation assistance for international talents
  • Wellbeing that works: Top-notch private healthcare (70% covered), 6-week second-parent leave, extra time off if your child is sick and needs you, and several prevention, health and wellbeing services on the Welii platform
  • A culture that cares: From inter-office trips to regular team events, there are plenty of ways to connect beyond your day-to-day. You'll also find active social, green, and LGBTQIA+ communities, plus Work Council benefits via Leeto, all here to support what matters to you, inside and outside of work

At Akeneo, you’ll be part of a supportive and collaborative team that values open communication, shared successes, and meaningful relationships.

The Team and Areas of Ownership

The SDM team owns the Akeneo Supplier Data Manager, the front door to the Akeneo Product Cloud for data.

SDM is a painkiller, not a vitamin. Retailers and distributors don't adopt it because it's nice to have; they adopt it because, without it, onboarding supplier data is a manual, error-prone job that keeps products off the shelf. Hundreds of suppliers send product data in various formats (spreadsheets, PDFs, images), and that data must be cleaned, classified, enriched, and verified before it reaches the catalogue. SDM does this through a pipeline of connected modules: mapping, validation, classification, extraction, multi-destination distribution, and more.

The scale is what makes this hard. These are not small files you can hand to an LLM and get a clean answer back. Supplier catalogues are large, constantly changing, and full of industry-specific terms, formatting quirks, and domain knowledge that trip up general-purpose tools. Some of the processing is deterministic; some of it isn't. Building systems that handle all of it reliably, at volume, across hundreds of supplier configurations, is the engineering problem you'd be here to help solve.

SDM is a cross-functional team that owns its work end-to-end and prides itself on solving the right problems, not just shipping code. Leadership sets direction and decides how much to invest in each problem; we own how to get there. When priorities compete, we make the trade-off together, grounded in customer data rather than opinion, and we're comfortable saying no to work that doesn't move the needle. The team is in a period of real investment and acceleration, and we're hiring engineers to help own SDM's future.

We're hiring at multiple levels on this team. This is the Software Engineer role for people on the rise. If you already have deep experience, our Senior Software Engineer opening is likely the better fit; you can always change once you speak to us.

Some steps are deterministic; some use LLMs to extract attributes and classify products. You'll help make them reliable, and you'll learn how to handle real problems of scale and correctness as you go.
  • Own what you build: as you grow, you'll take on more end-to-end, from shipping to monitoring in production to closing the loop with support. A weekly support rotation is shared across the team.

  • You care about the customer. You want to know who uses what you build and why it matters to them.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity, or want to get there. We won't hand you a detailed spec for everything. You'll get clear problems and the room to solve them, with support when you need it.
  • You use AI to think, not just to type. We build with tools like Claude Code. Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

We're hiring two Senior Quality Engineers to set up a Quality Engineering department at Lendable alongside a new Head of Quality.

At Lendable we already have a number of profitable, award winning credit products. They have a good automated quality story. However, as our customer base has grown into the millions we need to keep evolving to keep the quality bar high. Advances in AI engineering also have enabled us to ship faster, but we need to ensure we are not regressing on our quality metrics.

This is an automation-first role. You'll spend most of your time writing code - AI Agents, test frameworks, CI tooling, helpers. You won't be executing tests by hand. You'll work cross-functionally with software engineers, product and design. Quality is a team-level responsibility and your job is to work with teams to enable them to improve their quality processes by hands-on collaboration.

You'll also be working at the frontier of AI-assisted quality, using LLMs and AI tooling to speed up test authoring, triage failures, and surface coverage gaps, while applying the engineering judgement to keep tests trustworthy.

What you'll be doing

Enable teams to keep the quality bar high

  • Rotating around different product teams for short periods to level up quality

  • Define and evolve the pragmatic test pyramid for our products - deciding where E2E is worth the weight and where testing belongs in faster layers (unit and component tests)

  • Make deliberate calls about coverage, reliability, and speed trade-offs across our products

  • Devise and set up performance benchmarks to ensure critical parts of our systems don't regress

Bring AI testing into the SDLC

  • Speed up our SDLC by building agents that exploratory test changes and catch issues before they get to production

  • Use AI tools day-to-day to accelerate test authoring, cluster failures, surface coverage insights, and propose fixes

  • Decide where AI adds leverage and where a human eye is needed. A test suite that looks comprehensive but isn't trustworthy is worse than a smaller one we rely on

Build reliable E2E automation

  • Discover gaps in testing and help teams build comprehensive suites

  • Get test environments and data fixtures to a level where they are easy to use and reliable

  • Drive flakiness down and time-to-diagnosis down. We treat a flaky test the same way we treat a broken test, and we expect root-cause work rather than retry-until-green

Prevent defects, not just catch them

  • Partner with product and engineering on shift-left quality: join specs early, push back on ambiguous acceptance criteria, and surface risk before code is written

  • Close the loop on production issues using our observability stack (Datadog, Sentry, Grafana) - tying test coverage back to real customer impact

  • Ensure teams have Service Level Objectives set up and are achieving them

  • Run targeted exploratory testing on high-risk releases when it's the right call

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in quality engineering or test automation, with a track record of keeping automated suites stable rather than letting them rot into a graveyard of quarantined tests

  • Experience working in a scaled engineering environment with multiple teams pulling in different directions and priorities, and know how to navigate that to drive quality improvements across them

Resilience Care is a leading medical remote monitoring player and a clinical research partner. Founded in France in 2021, our mission is simple: improve patient care.
We build remote monitoring solutions in oncology, gastroenterology and psychiatry, powered by ePRO collection and AI techniques. Our platform helps care teams detect side effects early for continuous and proactive care, while our patient app helps people track and manage symptoms with tailored resources.
Our solutions optimize care pathways, enrich continuous patient understanding, and accelerate clinical research through the collection, structuring and detailed analysis of real-world data. Today, our solutions are deployed in routine care for 35,000 patients across 200+ healthcare institutions, and also support around twenty academic and industry clinical studies.
We put data at the service of care and therapeutic innovation, with the ambition to enable every patient to benefit from personalized medicine.

📝 Your role

In a nutshell: You join the Data Reliability Engineering (DRE) team to build, operate and secure the data platform that carries healthcare data from our production services to the people who use it — internal operational teams, clinical research users, and external partners receiving contractual data exports.

Your impact: Data arrives on time, complete, traceable and secure — and when it doesn't, we know before the users do. You turn one-off data requests and manual export procedures into automated, monitored, reproducible pipelines.

Your day-to-day:

  • Build and operate data pipelines : ingestion from application events & databases, transformation, export.

  • Build the tooling that handles those pipelines, hand in hand with SRE: infrastructure as code (Terraform, Helm on Kubernetes), deployment, CI/CD, secrets management, database operations and incident response.

  • Watch over data quality and pipeline health: Grafana dashboards, alerting, and metric- and log-based observability, so failures are detected and diagnosed fast.

  • Own data contracts and data quality: agree with the emitting squads on schemas, semantics and breaking-change rules, and enforce them with automated tests (freshness, completeness, referential integrity) that fail loudly before the data reaches its users.

  • Deliver secure data exports to external partners and institutions.

  • Provision and maintain dedicated PostgreSQL Research Spaces for clinical study teams, including access control and data scoping per study.

  • Help the modelers scale their work: industrialize the dbt project so a single modelisation written by a Data Analyst is centralized, parallelized and applied across several targets.

  • Work directly with the requesters: scope the need, challenge it, agree on what is feasible, deliver, and document.

  • Work with the product squads on the data they emit: challenge their design upstream, and take part in the implementation on their side (TypeScript) when needed — you contribute to their code, they keep their roadmap.

  • Participate in code reviews, technical design and continuous improvement of engineering standards.

✨ Your team

  • Your future teammates: Mélody Ballouard and Alric Gaurier — Data Reliability Engineers.

The team owns the data pipeline end to end: ingestion, transformation, exports, and the infrastructure underneath. You'll be exposed to all of it from day one.

  • ⚙️ You are the right person if you can:

    • Ship production-grade Python (tests, typing, code quality, reviews, CI), and use AI tools as a multiplier without letting go of engineering ownership.

    • Build and operate data pipelines and orchestration (Prefect, Airflow, Dagster or equivalent), including event streams (Kafka) and object/file transports (S3, SFTP).

Contexte

Le projet est né d'un besoin de gouvernance et d'audit réglementaire sur les APIs et les serveurs MCP, afin de maitriser leur référencement, les responsabilités, le cycle de vie et l’utilisation.

L'objectif est de construire un registre d’actifs numériques servant de source de référence a but de découvrabilité, de compréhensions des rôles, d’identifications des acteurs, des usages et des interconnections.

Un portail développeur viendra en complément du registre, afin de permettre son administration et son utilisation au quotidien : recherche et découverte d'actifs, consultation des informations et des relations. Accès aux contacts ainsi qu'à différents outils et ressources destinés aux développeurs.

Le projet est pensé dès sa conception comme un produit open source, générique et extensible, sans dépendance à un environnement d'entreprise particulier, afin de pouvoir être adopté, adapté et enrichi dans d'autres contextes.

La mission s'inscrit dans un contexte bancaire et sécurisé : les choix techniques doivent intégrer naturellement les exigences de sécurité, notamment sur l'usage des images et dépendances, la gestion des secrets, la journalisation et l'exposition des informations sensibles.

Objectifs de la prestation

La prestation vise à concevoir et développer le socle backend du registre : modèle de domaine, APIs d'administration et de consultation, mécanismes d'authentification et d'autorisation, gestion du cycle de vie des ressources, exposition OpenAPI et fondations techniques permettant une adoption open source. La prestation s'inscrit dans une démarche API First : les contrats d'API, leurs usages et leur documentation sont pensés comme des éléments structurants du produit, avant et pendant l'implémentation.

Missions

  • Participer à la clarification du besoin fonctionnel et métier autour du référencement, des responsabilités, du cycle de vie et des relations entre actifs numériques.
  • Concevoir les fonctionnalités dans une démarche API First, en travaillant les contrats, les usages, les erreurs, la documentation et la stabilité des interfaces dès les phases de conception.
  • Concevoir le modèle de domaine et le modèle de données du registre en tenant compte des APIs, serveurs MCP, responsable, contacts, tags, statuts, usages et relations.
  • Contribuer aux échanges de conception avec le profil frontend afin de garantir une bonne expérience développeur et une cohérence produit.
  • Structurer l'architecture backend selon des principes de clean architecture ou d'architecture hexagonale.
  • Mettre en place les mécanismes d'authentification, d'autorisation et de contrôle d'accès adaptés au produit.
  • Documenter les choix structurants, les conventions de contribution et les modalités d'exploitation du backend.
  • Développer les APIs backend avec NestJS et TypeScript, en appliquant des pratiques de conception d'API robustes, documentées et évolutives.
  • Produire et maintenir les contrats OpenAPI associés aux endpoints exposés.
  • Mettre en place les tests unitaires, tests d'intégration et pratiques de qualité nécessaires à un projet open source maintenable.

Expertises spécifiques attendues

  • NestJS et TypeScript.
  • Démarche API First : design de contrats, documentation, cohérence des ressources, versioning et expérience consommateur d'API.
  • API Design et conception d'APIs REST documentées et maintenables.
  • OpenAPI : conception, génération, validation ou publication de contrats.
  • Data Modeling et Domain Modeling.
  • Authentication / Authorization, idéalement dans des contextes OIDC / OAuth2 ou équivalents.
  • Tests backend : unitaires, intégration, éventuellement contract testing.
  • Architecture backend : clean architecture, architecture hexagonale, séparation domaine / application / infrastructure.
  • Culture open source : packaging, documentation, qualité de contribution, généricité et extensibilité.

Compétences transverses attendues

  • Être capable de challenger une décision, une idée ou une approche technique de manière constructive.
  • Être à l'aise avec la philosophie open source : lisibilité, documentation, généricité, extensibilité et contribution communautaire.
  • Utiliser l'IA comme outil de travail tout en restant capable d'expliquer, contrôler et assumer ce qui est produit.
  • Faire preuve de curiosité, apprendre vite et raisonner à partir du besoin pour construire une solution pertinente.
  • Avoir envie de construire un produit depuis zéro, avec une attention particulière à la maintenabilité et à la réutilisabilité hors contexte d'entreprise spécifique.
  • Penser la solution comme un produit open source générique et réutilisable, tout en vérifiant sa compatibilité avec les contraintes d'industrialisation de l'environnement afin d'éviter des blocages tardifs.
  • Anglais professionnel fortement recommandé, notamment pour échanger avec les équipes de production au Portugal lorsque cela est nécessaire.

Livrables attendus

  • Code source backend maintenable, testé et documenté.
  • Contrats OpenAPI et documentation d'utilisation des APIs.
  • Modèle de domaine et modèle de données documentés.
  • Tests automatisés et éléments d'intégration continue associés.
  • Documentation technique, guide de contribution et éléments facilitant l'installation locale.
  • Recommandations d'architecture et justification des principaux choix techniques.
